claims.text: The Stoa of Attalos is a magnificent covered walkway or portico located prominently on the east side of the Ancient Agora.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was built around 150 BC and named after King Attalos II of Pergamon, who generously gifted it to the city of Athens.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The king donated the building in gratitude for the excellent education he had received in Athens under the philosopher Carneades.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The original building was in frequent use for centuries until its woodwork was tragically burned by the Heruli invaders in 267 AD.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: What you see today is an incredibly accurate reconstruction completed from 1952 to 1956, largely funded by American donors including John D. Rockefeller Jr.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The impressive reconstructed building currently houses the Museum of the Ancient Agora, with exhibits primarily connected to Athenian democracy.
claims.subject: self
